sentences.text:
Vishnu Parte vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 October,
2025
 Neutral Citation No. 2025:Mphc-Jbp:50756
 1 
 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
At Jabalpur

Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Pramod Kumar Agrawal

On The 8 th Of October, 2025
 Misc. Criminal Case No. 40772 of 2025
 Vishnu Parte
 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh And Others
 Appearance:
 Shri Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari - Advocate for the applicant
 Ms. Ranjana Agnihotri - Dy. Government Advocate for St
 Order

This is the second bail application filed by the applicant under Section 483 of BNSS for grant of regular bail relating to Crime No.55/2024 registered at Police Station Malajkhand, District Balaghat (M.P.) under Sections 363, 366(A), 365, 343, 376(3), 376(2) of IPC and Section 3/4, 5L/6, 16/17 of POCSO Act.
Applicant is in detention since 21.03.2024.
His earlier bail application was dismissed as withdrawn.
2. As per the prosecution story, allegation against the applicant is of kidnapping the minor prosecutrix and committing rape upon her.
After investigation, offence under the aforesaid sections has been registered against the applicant.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that applicant has falsely been implicated in the present case.
The applicant is in jail since 21.03.2024.

He has drawn the attention of this Court to the statements of mother of the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:50756 2 MCRC-40772-2025 prosecutrix and has submitted that at the time of incident prosecutrix was major and prosecutrix has not supported the prosecution story.
Conclusion of the trial will take considerable time, therefore, it has been prayed that the applicant may be released on bail.
4. On the other hand, learned counsel for State has opposed the grant of bail to the applicant and submitted that at the time of incident, prosecutrix was minor.
Applicant is aged about 32 years.
Despite being married and having two wives, applicant has committed rape with the minor prosecutrix.
It is further submitted that at this stage, minute appreciation of evidence cannot be done.
Hence, he prayed for rejection of this bail application.

7. Looking to the overall facts and circumstances of the case as well as seriousness of offence, I am not inclined to grant bail to the applicant.
8. Accordingly, the application is dismissed.
